body:
FOUND BY DRIVING THE CLI END TO END, 2026-08-19, during T186. The unit rails did not catch it and
that is the lesson: they asserted that law BOUND and never that it SERVED.

MEASURED, on two live stores with different operator keys:

    $ loam federate open --from http://127.0.0.1:5821/default --into friends --prefix alice --home bob
    loam: channel channel:friends:alice
      6 accepted, 0 already held, of 6 offered
      bound alice:Note

    $ curl .../graphql -d '{"query":"{ __schema { queryType { fields { name } } } }"}'
    {"data":{"__schema":{"queryType":{"fields":[{"name":"alice_Note"},{"name":"alice_Notes"}]}}}}

    $ curl .../graphql -d '{"query":"{ alice_Note(entity: \"note:hi\") { title } }"}'
    {"data":{"alice_Note":{"title":null}}}

The FIELD is served — law bound correctly, under the receiver's prefix, exactly as §46 designs. The
DATA does not resolve. The lens gathers over the receiving store's PRIMARY GROUND, and a channel's
deltas live in its pool, which is a separate ground by design (§46 criterion 15, and the reason
`drop` stays a physical purge rather than a filtered delete).

So §46 criterion 4 is HALF met. It says law "binds at the living name `alice:Post` AND serves at the
GraphQL field the door derives from it". Binding lands; serving does not. User story S5 — "Myk
queries alice:Post and gets Alice's data" — does not work today.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN TICKET rather than a fixup on T186. `RequestContext` carries only `actor`; there
is no container-scoped read path. Making a channel-bound lens resolve over its pool changes how the
GraphQL door gathers, which is a read-path change with a blast radius across every door. That is a
design decision, not a repair, and it wants Myk.

WHAT IT MUST NOT BE: mirroring the peer's deltas into the receiver's primary ground. That would make
reads work in one line and destroy criterion 15, and with it the proof that severing a peer is a
physical purge rather than a filter. The isolation is load-bearing; the read path is what must move.

THE SHAPE THAT LOOKS RIGHT (for the working spec, not decided): a lens bound from a channel records
the container it came from, and its gather is evaluated over `containerScope(that container)` rather
than the primary ground. That keeps every existing lens resolving exactly as it does now — the
scoped path is entered only by law that arrived through a channel.

RAILS:
1. The e2e that found this: two stores, different operator keys, `federate open`, then a GraphQL read
   of the peer's data through the receiver's own surface returns the VALUE, not null.
2. Two-sided: a receiver's OWN lens still resolves over the primary ground and is unaffected.
3. Criterion 15 still holds after the fix — the peer's deltas are still absent from the primary
   ground. A fix that satisfies rail 1 by mirroring must fail this one.
4. Fan-in: two channels' lenses resolve over their OWN pools, not over each other's.

TIER: Myk's merge — it changes how the read path gathers.

SETTLED BY MYK IN CHAT, 2026-08-19 (late). The fix is now SMALL and the design question is closed.

THE ERROR THAT MADE THIS LOOK BIG WAS MINE: I conflated STORAGE with VISIBILITY. Criterion 15 says a
peer's bytes are not in the receiving store's PRIMARY GROUND. It says nothing about what a query may
gather. Myk's framing settles it — a delta's canonical location and a reader's scope are different
questions, so a container-scoped read does not weaken criterion 15 at all.

THE FIX: the query path gathers containerScope of the container being queried, instead of the raw
primary ground. Bob reads the container he opened the channel into, and alice's data resolves. This
connects to SPEC 39's existing rule that a connection binds to exactly one container — the binding IS
the query's scope.

WHAT MUST NOT WIDEN, and this is the decision Myk reasoned to himself and then confirmed: THE BASE
GATHER EXCLUDES DESCENDANTS. A container shows its own contents; descent is EXPLICIT and
rights-checked. Three things break under descendants-included, and he found the multi-tenant one:
- quarantine (SPEC 24) leaks into ordinary reads, and a default needing exceptions carved out of it
  is the wrong default;
- tenant isolation becomes opt-out — it would depend on the operator not querying root, which is
  etiquette rather than isolation;
- creating a container silently changes what EXISTING queries answer.
The filesystem analogy that made descendants-included feel intuitive argues the other way: ls / does
not recurse, and descent is permission-gated.

INBOXES ARE NOT AN EXCEPTION. containerScope composes inbox pools upward because inboxOf means "I am
this container's STORAGE", while parent means "I am a container INSIDE it". SPEC 39.3 says why the
mechanism exists: a membership Term cannot reach a separate pool. So a federation pool declared
inboxOf a receiving container is PART OF it — the receiver created it to receive peers — and is not
part of root.

RAILS unchanged from above, plus one the decision earns:
5. The base gather still EXCLUDES a declared child container (parent), while still composing an inbox
   pool (inboxOf). Two-sided in one rail, because that distinction IS the safety property, and a fix
   that gathered both would look correct on every federation test.
title: Channel-bound law binds but does not serve — the read path gathers the primary ground only
